mainTopic: The source of the סוטה dust, whether ashes may replace it, and רבי ישמעאל's list of places where the הלכה goes beyond the פסוק
overview: The גמרא finishes איסי בן יהודה's list of places where the משכן stood, showing that the סוטה dust is taken from the Sanctuary floor wherever it is. איסי בן מנחם says no פסוק is needed for this, since a קל וחומר teaches it. He reads 'בקרקע המשכן' as teaching that the dust must come from the floor itself, not from a basket. The גמרא then asks whether ashes may be used if there is no dust. It explains that this question only arises according to בית הלל. To answer it, the גמרא brings רבי ישמעאל's list of three places where the הלכה goes beyond the פסוק: dust for covering blood, a נזיר's razor, and the scroll of a גט. Since סוטה is not on the list, it seems ashes are not allowed. The גמרא answers that the list is not complete and points to the מצורע, who shaves his whole body even though the פסוק, read as a כלל ופרט וכלל, seems narrower. רב נחמן בר יצחק, רב פפא and רב אשי then each explain why רבי ישמעאל did not count the מצורע.

steps.title: The places where the Sanctuary stood
steps.stepSummary: The end of איסי בן יהודה's list: שילה, נוב, גבעון, and the בית המקדש in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שילה, נוב, גבעון, and the Eternal House.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list that began just before this, naming every place the Sanctuary ever stood. The point is that the dust for the סוטה is taken from the Sanctuary floor wherever the Sanctuary is located.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה uses the words 'בקרקע המשכן' to teach that the rule was not only for the desert. Any later home of the Sanctuary counts, up to the permanent בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Shiloh, where the מִשְׁכָּן stood after the Jews entered the Land
Nob, a later location of the מִשְׁכָּן
Gibeon, another later location of the מִשְׁכָּן
The 'Eternal House', the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ in יְרוּשָׁלַיִם

phrases.english: Shiloh, Nob, and Gibeon,
and the Eternal House.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement of איסי בן יהודה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dust for the סוטה comes from the Sanctuary floor in every place where the Sanctuary stood, including the בית המקדש.

steps.title: איסי בן מנחם learns it from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן מנחם says the פסוק is not needed. A קל וחומר from the lighter rule of טומאה in the Sanctuary already teaches that location makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בן מנחם says: It is not needed. If for a light impurity the Torah made no distinction, then for the serious impurity of a married woman, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא, איסי בן מנחם, disagrees with how איסי בן יהודה learned the rule. He says we can work it out by logic, a קל וחומר, without any פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on entering the Sanctuary while impure is 'light', since a בית דין gives no death penalty for it. Yet it applies wherever the Sanctuary stands. The sin of a married woman is 'serious', so its rules must surely apply wherever the Sanctuary stands too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed: no פָּסוּק is required to teach this
A 'light' impurity: entering the מִקְדָּשׁ while impure
The Torah made no distinction (between locations)
The 'impurity' of a married woman who sinned with another man
All the more so: the conclusion of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two תנאים agreeing on the הלכה while disagreeing on its source. That frees up the words 'בקרקע המשכן' for a different teaching.

phrases.english: Isi ben Menachem says,
It is not needed:
Now, if with a light impurity,
phrases.notes: He means going into the Sanctuary while impure. It is 'light' because בית דין doesn't give a death penalty for it.

phrases.english: the Torah made no distinction,
then with the serious impurity of a married woman,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסִי בֶּן מְנַחֵם אוֹמֵר, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source (a קל וחומר) for the same halacha that איסי בן יהודה learned from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר, the סוטה dust is taken from the Sanctuary wherever it stands; no פסוק is needed.

steps.title: What the words 'floor of the Sanctuary' teach instead
steps.stepSummary: If the קל וחומר already teaches the location rule, the words 'בקרקע המשכן' teach that the dust must come from the floor itself, not from the כהן's own basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'on the floor of the Sanctuary'? To teach that he may not bring the dust from his own basket.
steps.whatsHappening: איסי בן מנחם answers the obvious question about his view: if logic teaches the rule, why did the Torah write 'בקרקע המשכן'? He gives those words a new job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the words are no longer needed for 'any location', they teach that the dust must actually come from the Sanctuary floor. The כהן cannot bring dust from home in a container and put it straight into the water.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פָּסוּק come to teach?
On the floor of the Sanctuary (במדבר 5:17)
His basket or container

steps.whatToRemember: איסי בן יהודה: 'בקרקע המשכן' means wherever the Sanctuary is. איסי בן מנחם: that comes from a קל וחומר, and 'בקרקע המשכן' means the dust must come from the floor, not a basket.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying
"on the floor of the Sanctuary"?
That he should not bring it from his basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the פסוק is for, now that the location rule comes from the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the קל וחומר teaches the location rule, the words 'בקרקע המשכן' would seem to be extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words teach that the dust must be taken from the floor itself, not brought in a basket.

steps.title: If there is no dust, may ashes be used?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask: if no dust is found on the Sanctuary floor, may ashes be put into the סוטה water instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If there is no dust there, may one put in ashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question with איבעיא להו. It asks what to do when there is no dust on the floor, and whether ashes can take its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'עפר', dust. The question is whether ashes can count as 'עפר' for the סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חֲכָמִים)
Dust or earth
Ashes
What is the law?

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If there is no dust there,
what is the law about putting in ashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: replacing the required dust with ashes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ashes may replace dust in the סוטה water when no dust is available.

steps.title: No question according to בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: According to בית שמאי there is no question, because they hold that ashes are never called 'עפר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to בית שמאי you need not ask, since they say: We never find ashes called 'dust.'
steps.whatsHappening: Before tackling the question, the גמרא narrows it. It says the question cannot be asked according to בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that ashes are never called 'עפר' in the Torah. So when the Torah says 'עפר' for the סוטה, ashes are clearly not allowed in their view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of
You need not ask (the answer is obvious)
The school of שַׁמַּאי
We have not found (anywhere in the Torah)

phrases.english: According to Beis Shammai,
you need not ask,
since they say: We never find ashes that are called "dust."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question by showing it does not arise in בית שמאי's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out asking the question according to בית שמאי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For בית שמאי the answer is obvious: ashes are never 'עפר', so they cannot be used.

steps.title: The real question according to בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל hold that ashes can be called 'עפר'. Even so, maybe 'בקרקע המשכן' requires real earth, or maybe those words are only there for איסי בן יהודה's or איסי בן מנחם's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question is according to בית הלל, who say we do find ashes called 'dust.' What is the law? Even though ashes are called 'dust,' here it says 'on the floor of the Sanctuary.' Or perhaps those words come only to teach like איסי בן יהודה or איסי בן מנחם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the real question, according to בית הלל, and sets out both sides. The next step brings a source to try to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: 'בקרקע המשכן' hints that the material must come from the ground, so only real dust works, even though ashes are sometimes called 'עפר'. Side two: those words are already used, for איסי בן יהודה's 'any location' or איסי בן מנחם's 'not from a basket', so they say nothing about ashes, and ashes would be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Where you should ask the question
The school of הִלֵּל
Even though
Or perhaps: introduces the other side of a question
For the teaching of

steps.confusionAlert: 'Or perhaps it comes for איסי בן יהודה or איסי בן מנחם' does not mean they discussed ashes. It means the words are already used for their teachings, so they can't also teach that dust is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a פסוק that is 'used up' by one teaching may not be available to teach another rule.

phrases.english: Where you should ask,
is according to Beis Hillel, who say:
We do find ashes that are called "dust." What is the law?
phrases.notes: For example, the ashes of the פרה אדומה are called עפר in במדבר 19:17.

phrases.english: Even though they are called "dust,"
here it is written "on the floor of the Sanctuary,"
or perhaps this "on the floor of the Sanctuary"
comes for the teaching of Isi ben Yehuda
or for the teaching of Isi ben Menachem?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, אַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית הִלֵּל דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out בית שמאי, states the real question according to בית הלל and gives both sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to בית הלל, does 'בקרקע המשכן' require real dust, or is it used up by the teachings of איסי בן יהודה and איסי בן מנחם, so that ashes would be allowed?

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's three places where the halacha goes beyond the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי ישמעאל's teaching. In three places the Torah names one specific thing, but the הלכה allows anything: covering blood with 'dust,' a נזיר's 'razor,' and a גט written on a 'scroll.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל that in three places the הלכה goes around the plain words of the פסוק. The Torah says 'dust,' but the הלכה allows anything. The Torah says 'razor,' but the הלכה includes anything. The Torah says 'scroll,' but the הלכה allows anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a proof to answer the open question about ashes. It sets up a list that it will use in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל gives an exact number: three places where the הלכה goes beyond the words of the פסוק. Each case on the list is one where the Torah names a specific item but the הלכה widens it. The proof will depend on the fact that סוטה is not one of the three.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to try to answer a question
The הלכה goes around the verse: the tradition rules differently from the plain words
Razor (the נזיר may not remove his hair)
Scroll or document (the Torah's word for a גט)

steps.whyThisMatters: A list with an exact number suggests it is complete. That is the whole basis of the proof.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
In three places the halacha bypasses the verse.
The Torah said "with dust,"
phrases.notes: This is about covering the blood after slaughtering a wild animal or bird (ויקרא 17:13).

phrases.english: but the halacha is: with anything.
The Torah said "with a razor,"
phrases.notes: This is the נזיר, who may not cut his hair (במדבר 6:5).

phrases.english: but the halacha is: with anything.
The Torah said "a scroll,"
phrases.notes: This is the גט, the divorce document (דברים 24:1).

phrases.english: but the halacha is: on anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer the question from step 6 about using ashes.
steps.raayaObject: Whether ashes may be used in place of dust for the סוטה water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי ישמעאל: a numbered list of three places where the הלכה goes beyond the verse.

steps.title: If ashes worked, סוטה should be on the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the proof. If ashes could replace dust for סוטה, then רבי ישמעאל should have counted this as a fourth case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is true that ashes are allowed, let him count this case too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the list to argue that ashes cannot be used for the סוטה water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering blood is listed even though the Torah says 'dust,' because the הלכה allows anything. If the same were true by סוטה, it would fit the list perfectly. Since it is missing, it seems the הלכה does not allow ashes there.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so: introduces 'if your idea were right, then...'
Let him count it (on the list)

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if ashes really could be used in place of dust for the סוטה water.

phrases.english: let him count this one too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the list in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility (step 6) that ashes count as dust for סוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A numbered list implies it is complete. סוטה is missing from it, so the הלכה must not go beyond 'dust' there.

steps.title: The list is not complete
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל taught some cases and left others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by saying the list of three was never meant to be complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the list is complete. By saying רבי ישמעאל left cases out, the גמרא removes the proof that ashes are not allowed, at least for now. The next step challenges this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught and left over: the list is not complete

phrases.english: He taught and left some out.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that the list is complete.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number 'three' means these are the only cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל did not list every case, so leaving out סוטה proves nothing.

steps.title: What else was left out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he left out סוטה, what other case did he leave out? It is hard to say a list leaves out only one item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what else did he leave out, that we should say he left out this one too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer 'he left some out' by asking for another missing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that if you say a list is not complete, you need to show at least one other missing case. If סוטה were the only missing case, he would simply have added it, so the answer would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What else did he leave out, that he left out this one? This asks for a second missing case

phrases.english: And what else did he leave out, that he left out this one?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the list is not complete.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A list that leaves out just one case is not believable. Without another missing case, the answer does not hold.

steps.title: He also left out the מצורע's shaving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל also left out the מצורע. It quotes a ברייתא that reads the verse about the מצורע's shaving as a general rule, a detail, and a general rule again. So he shaves every place where hair gathers together and can be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left out the מצורע, as a ברייתא teaches: 'And on the seventh day he shall shave all his hair' is a general rule. 'His head, his beard, and his eyebrows' is a detail. 'And all his hair he shall shave' repeats the general rule. With a general rule, a detail, and a general rule, you include only things like the detail. The detail names places where hair gathers together and is seen, so every place where hair gathers together and is seen must be shaved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names a second case that רבי ישמעאל left out, the shaving of a מצורע. It begins quoting a ברייתא to explain the verse there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a second case is missing, 'he left some out' becomes a believable answer, and the proof against ashes would fall away. So far the ברייתא only builds the reading of the verse with the כלל ופרט וכלל method. Step 13 shows how the הלכה goes beyond this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who shaves his hair as part of becoming pure
A general rule, then a detail, then a general rule again: a method for reading פסוקים
Similar to the detail: only things like the listed examples are included
A gathering of hair that can be seen

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא has already shown the הלכה going beyond the verse. Here it only explains what the verse itself means. The part about the הלכה comes after this.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא proposes the מצורע as a second case missing from רבי ישמעאל's list. If that holds, the list is not complete and cannot prove that ashes are not allowed. Steps 14–16 then question whether the מצורע really counts as an omission.

phrases.english: He left out the metzora,
as it is taught in a baraita:
"And it shall be on the seventh day
he shall shave all his hair": this is a general rule,
"his head and his beard
and his eyebrows": this is a detail,
"and all his hair he shall shave":
it went back and stated a general rule.
A general rule, a detail, and a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may include only what is similar to the detail.
Just as the detail is clearly
a place where hair gathers and is visible,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל מָקוֹם כִּינּוּס שֵׂעָר וְנִרְאֶה.
phrases.english: so too every place where hair gathers and is visible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by naming another case left out of the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names a second case missing from the list, so the list is clearly not complete.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סוטה would be the only case missing, which is not believable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצורע is offered as another missing case, which would show the list is not complete. Steps 14–16 then explain why רבי ישמעאל may have left it out on purpose.

steps.title: What the rule for the מצורע's shaving includes and leaves out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its כלל ופרט וכלל reading. It includes pubic hair, and it leaves out armpit hair and hair on the rest of the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this rule add? It adds pubic hair. What does it leave out? It leaves out armpit hair and the hair of the whole body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא from step 11. It spells out which hair the מצורע must shave and which he does not have to shave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the מצורע shaves hair that grows in a cluster and can be seen. Pubic hair fits both conditions, so it is included. Armpit hair is hidden, and body hair is spread out, so both are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: included, added (a case that the rule brings in)
excluded, left out (a case that the rule keeps out)
pubic hair (a polite way of saying it)
the armpit

phrases.english: What did it include?
It included the pubic hair.
What did it exclude?
It excluded the hair of the armpit
and the hair of his whole body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 11 by stating what the כלל ופרט וכלל includes and what it leaves out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the פסוק alone, the מצורע shaves only hair that is clustered and visible. This includes pubic hair but not armpit hair or general body hair.

steps.title: The הלכה says the מצורע shaves his whole body
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that the מצורע shaves like a smooth gourd. A משנה says the razor goes over all his flesh, and that the second shaving is the same as the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is that he shaves until he is smooth like a gourd. A משנה teaches that when the כהן comes to shave the מצורע, he passes a razor over all of his flesh. The end of that משנה teaches that on the seventh day he shaves him a second time, just like the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the actual הלכה goes past what the ברייתא read from the פסוק. The מצורע shaves everything, even armpit and body hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's reading of the פסוק left out armpit and body hair. The משנה says the second shaving matches the first, and the first one covers all his flesh. So the הלכה goes beyond the reading of the פסוק, which makes the מצורע look like another case רבי ישמעאל left off his list.

keyTerms.meaning: he shaves like a gourd, meaning completely smooth
to shave
a razor
the end part of a משנה or ברייתא
a shaving

phrases.english: And the halacha is: he shaves like a gourd.
phrases.notes: A gourd is smooth all over. So it means nothing is left unshaved.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
When he comes to shave the metzora,
he passes a razor over all of his flesh,
and it teaches in the latter part:
and on the seventh day he shaves him,
the second shaving like the first shaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the actual הלכה against the reading in step 12. This shows the מצורע is a case where הלכה goes past the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The claim from step 11 that the מצורע is another case רבי ישמעאל left off his list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נגעים: the razor passes over all his flesh, and the second shaving is like the first.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two shavings. The ברייתא's narrow reading is about the seventh-day shaving. The משנה is needed to show that even that second shaving covers the whole body.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the הלכה here only overrides a דרשה of the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל only counted cases where הלכה overrides the פסוק itself. Here the הלכה only overrides a rabbinic reading, the כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבי ישמעאל only counted cases where the הלכה passes over the פסוק itself. This case only passes over a teaching of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains why the מצורע is not on רבי ישמעאל's list: it is a different kind of case. That means the מצורע is not really a case 'left out', which weakens the answer 'he taught and left some out' from steps 9–11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In dust, razor, and scroll, the פסוק itself names one specific thing, and the הלכה goes past it. With the מצורע, the narrow rule came from a דרשה of the חכמים, not from the plain words of the פסוק. So the הלכה is only overriding that דרשה, and the case does not fit the list.

keyTerms.meaning: bypasses, goes around (the הלכה goes past something)
the פסוק itself
from the חכמים (here, their דרשה)
he is counting

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
When he counted,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי ישמעאל, making his list of three cases.

phrases.english: it was cases where the halacha bypasses a verse;
this one bypasses a teaching of the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: He means the כלל ופרט וכלל reading from step 11, which is a דרשה of the חכמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כִּי קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the מצורע from steps 11-13 is not on רבי ישמעאל's list. If it was left out on purpose, it is not really a case 'left out', which weakens step 11's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the list's category more narrowly, so the case falls outside it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצורע is a case where הלכה goes past the פסוק, so רבי ישמעאל should have counted it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only covers cases where הלכה overrides the plain פסוק. Here it only overrides a rabbinic דרשה, so the case was rightly left out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי ישמעאל omitted the מצורע from his list.

steps.title: רב פפא: the הלכה here adds to the פסוק and does not uproot it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל only counted cases where הלכה bypasses and uproots the פסוק. With the מצורע, the הלכה bypasses and adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבי ישמעאל only counted cases where the הלכה passes over the פסוק and uproots it. This case passes over the פסוק and adds to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different reason why the מצורע is not on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In dust, razor, and scroll, the הלכה cancels the limit of the פסוק, since other materials or tools work too. With the מצורע, the clustered, visible hair the פסוק requires still gets shaved, and the הלכה just adds the rest of the body. Adding is not uprooting, so it is a different kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: uproots, cancels what the פסוק said
adds on to what the פסוק said

steps.whatToRemember: The מצורע's full-body shaving is not on רבי ישמעאל's list. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it only overrides a rabbinic דרשה. רב פפא says it only adds to the פסוק and does not uproot it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
When he counted,
it was cases where the halacha bypasses and uproots;
this one bypasses and adds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כִּי קָא חָשֵׁיב הֲלָכָה עוֹקֶבֶת וְעוֹקֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question that רב נחמן בר יצחק answered in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the list's category differently: only cases where the הלכה uproots the פסוק are included.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any case where הלכה goes past the פסוק should be on רבי ישמעאל's list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only cases where the הלכה uproots the פסוק count. The מצורע's shaving only adds, so it is not on the list.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two different ways to understand what רבי ישמעאל's list is about: where the overridden rule comes from (רב נחמן בר יצחק), or how the הלכה changes the פסוק (רב פפא).

steps.title: רב אשי: the limiting ברייתא is רבי ישמעאל's own view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא that reads the מצורע's shaving as a כלל ופרט וכלל, limiting it to visible places where hair gathers, follows רבי ישמעאל, who learns פסוקים that way. So the question from רבי ישמעאל's list does not start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is רבי ישמעאל's, because he learns פסוקים through general rules and details.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to why רבי ישמעאל left the מצורע out of his list. He says the ברייתא that limits the shaving is רבי ישמעאל's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the הלכה says the מצורע shaves his whole body, even though the פסוק, read as a כלל ופרט וכלל, limits it. רב אשי says that limited reading is exactly how רבי ישמעאל learns, since he reads פסוקים through כללי ופרטי. So for רבי ישמעאל the shaving follows that limited reading, and there was no case here for him to count.

keyTerms.meaning: A later אמורא who gives a new answer here
Here it means the ברייתא quoted in Steps 11-12, not the משנה
Whose is it? Which תנא does this follow?
General rules and details, a way of learning פסוקים
He learns out of the פסוק, he interprets

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers for why רבי ישמעאל did not count the מצורע: (1) the הלכה only overrides a rabbinic reading, (2) the הלכה adds and does not uproot, (3) רב אשי: the limiting ברייתא is רבי ישמעאל's own view.
steps.confusionAlert: Here מַתְנִיתָא means the ברייתא from Steps 11-12, which limits the shaving. It does not mean the משנה from Step 13, which says the razor goes over all his flesh.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This baraita, whose opinion is it?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from before that limits the shaving to visible places where hair gathers.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yishmael's,
who interprets verses through generalizations and details.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָא מַתְנִיתָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer, alongside Steps 14 and 15, to the question of why רבי ישמעאל left out the מצורע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: names the תנא behind the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limiting ברייתא is a general reading, and the הלכה of shaving the whole body bypasses it even for רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limiting ברייתא is רבי ישמעאל's own view through כללי ופרטי, so there was no case for him to count.
